scope: TCAS-II C1/C2 mechanism rebuild; frozen Motion C12 ep34; deep research and CPU evidence, not novelty or acceptance certification

search_families: product/result sparsity and small-state differential SNN execution
Gustavson/broadcast/common-subexpression reductions and strong single-source controls
PSN exact threshold bounds and prior early termination
Motion-XOR temporal K pairing and attention I/O
stop_reason: Direct prior-art mechanisms and stronger cost controls now determine the ranking. The remaining decision-changing gaps require new causal timing, port models, broader frozen workloads and matched physical implementation, rather than more generic paper search.
unresolved: cheap causal C2 selector and capture-only requests
C1 slot and extra weight-delivery timing
matched VCS/DC/PT/Formality/P&R for any new mechanism
